alana: quick check-in: I ran the fused-attn qkv packing + postproc microbench on rw-medium. seeing a regression at seq=1024 for batch=8, ~6% p50 higher. anyone else?
jit: saw that too on the 2xA100 pool earlier today. looks like epilogue path gets L2-thrashed when we do bias+rope in the same kernel.
rohit: can you paste the profile? nvprof / nsight summaries would help.
alana: paste of perf summary: ```
# perf summary
seq=1024 batch=8 model=lm-small fused=qkv+post
p50: baseline=12.4ms fused=13.2ms (+6.5%)
p95: baseline=24.8ms fused=25.0ms (+0.8%)
SM Util: baseline=78% fused=81%
DRAM BW: fused +9%```
bench-bot: auto-bench report: https://bench.internal/2249801234 - added comparisons (packed vs split-kernel). note: packed variant higher throughput at seq<=512, worse at 1024+.
kevin: hypothesis: packing moves more data into shared/L2 between qkv unpack + epilogue; good for small seq due to reduced kernel launches, but at large seq it increases working set and evicts prefetch lines.
liz: that matches flame graphs i captured — fused kernel has a long epilogue loop with more scattered loads for rotary/bias. I can share the annotated nvprof later.
jit: can we try keeping QKV pack but split epilogue into a tiny final kernel? i.e., pack+main-attn fused, then lightweight epilogue that applies bias+rope+outproj. avoids large register pressure in main kernel.
rohit: yes, that was our earlier 'split-ep' experiment. I have a branch with split-ep and prefetch hints. micro numbers: seq=1024 batch=8 -> p50=12.6ms (almost baseline). but extra kernel launch + cudaMemcpy overhead minimal.
alana: code snippet of the split plan: ```
// fused main (qkv pack + attn compute)
launch fused_attn_packed_main(..., out_intermediate);
// epilogue light
launch fused_epilogue_small(out_intermediate, rotary, bias, out_final);
```
kevin: also try using __ldg for bias loads and hoist rotary trig lookups into shared memory for lane groups. that reduced stray memory ops in prior patches.
liz: another angle: adaptive path chooser in runtime — prefer packed+fused for seq<=512, switch to split-ep for seq>512. we already have kernel chooser hooks that look at seq distribution; easiest to add a rule.
jit: agree. runtime rule pseudocode: ```
if seq<=512 and batch<=16 -> use packed-fused
else -> use packed+split-ep
```
rohit: gotcha: need to account for KV cache paged behavior — split-ep touches cache writebacks differently. when paged-kv is enabled, epilogue kernel fragmentation can increase CUDA memcpys. bench with paged-kv on/off.
alana: I re-ran with paged-kv=on: fused p50 +9% at 1024, split-ep p50 +1%. with paged-kv=off: fused +4%, split-ep ~0%. so paged-kv amplifies the regression.
kevin: probably because packed-fused writes larger contiguous pages and the epilogue's extra kernel causes better alignment, reducing thrash. weird. need flame graphs comparing global memory stores.
bench-bot: attached artifacts: /artifacts/2249801234/{nvprof.txt,flame_fused.svg,flame_split.svg,bench_table.csv}
liz: suggested next steps: 1) land runtime kernel chooser with conservative thresholds 2) iterate on fused kernel to reduce epilogue working set (try shared memory buffering for rotary/bias) 3) retest with realistic arrival distributions not just static batch sizes 4) add an A/B in canary to measure tail impact.
rohit: small TODOs: - push split-ep branch for internal review - add a microbench variant that simulates paged-kv eviction pattern - instrument load/store counts into perf counters
jit: I'll add a quick wrapper in the scheduler to emit metric: chosen_kernel, seq, batch, p50, p95 so we can correlate on prod.
alana: thanks. i'm going to rollback the experimental default (we'd flipped to packed-fused in last deploy) to avoid regressing heavy seq workloads. re-deploy in 10m.
kevin: sounds good. also add a NOTE in the changelog: "reverted packed-fused default for seq>512 due to epilogue L2 thrash".
liz: leaving a comment with the nvprof excerpt and a short flame image in thread. :eyes:
rohit: if anyone wants to pair on shared-buffering optimization tomorrow ping me.
alana: great, closing for now. we'll re-open once runtime chooser + split-ep lands. :thumbsup:
